question_text: Evaluate publishing an easy-to-use ML flood-risk predictor for the public when its estimates have uncertainty and the training data cover some districts better than others.
adaptation_rationale: Retain public-deployment decision, explicitly about ML transparency/equity/misinformation. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
solution: Public access may improve preparedness and transparency, but uneven data coverage can produce unfairly unreliable advice. Users may treat uncertain estimates as guarantees, causing harm or misinformation. Publishing uncertainty, coverage limitations and clear guidance can support informed use; release should depend on adequate validation and honest communication.

marking_points.criterion: Weighs a practical mitigation such as clear limitations/coverage disclosure.
Supported judgement balancing benefits and harms.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent technically correct answers meeting the same scoped requirement; valid alternative algorithms accepted where they meet any explicit question constraints.
partial_credit_notes: Award each specified criterion independently up to the allocation. Credit correct method after an earlier slip when consistent; do not award the same point twice.

verification.technical: Independently solved; compared relevant source MS points, with obsolete/source-error assertions not imported.
verification.code_execution: No executable code required; explicit answer/trace checked manually.
